spot.html_text: But “The Lived-Experience of the Black Man” is really the key chapter in the book. In that chapter, Fanon deploys the conceptual tools developed in previous chapters in order to debunk the remaining legacies of racial essentialism. A good bit of this was undertaken in the first chapter, where Fanon critically reads Aimé Césaire and his articulation of Négritude around the question of language.
